colors.name: Ink Black
colors.role: Primary text, heading fills, primary borders, and the structural ink color across all UI surfaces

colors.name: Pure White
colors.role: Default page canvas, card surfaces, button text on dark fills, and outlined-button fills

colors.name: Carbon
colors.role: Filled primary action background, hard offset shadow color, and high-contrast icon fills

colors.name: Cream Paper
colors.role: Warm hero band, footer surface, and the signature alternate canvas that gives Coda its editorial mood

colors.name: Ash Border
colors.role: Hairline borders, card edges, and subtle dividers separating surfaces from canvas

colors.name: Graphite
colors.role: Secondary body text, muted helper text, and low-emphasis metadata

colors.name: Smoke
colors.role: Tertiary text, placeholder text, disabled labels, and nav item resting state

colors.name: Slate Button
colors.role: Secondary button borders and mid-weight icon strokes

colors.name: Ember Orange
colors.role: Sole chromatic accent - heading highlights, section eyebrow text, decorative underlines, and brand-mark punctuation. The single warm note against an otherwise black-and-cream system

fonts.name: Calibre-R
fonts.role: Display and section headlines. Custom geometric 700-weight face with extremely tight tracking that compresses letterforms into dense blocks of ink. The heavy + tight combination is Coda's signature - headlines feel carved rather than written. Substitute: Manrope 800 or DM Sans 800 with -0.03em tracking.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.role: All UI text: body copy, nav links, buttons, labels, captions. Inter carries the entire functional layer; its near-default weights and tracking let the Calibre headlines lead.

fonts.name: Tiempos-Headline
fonts.role: Occasional editorial subheading in a light serif weight - the soft counterpoint to Calibre's blocky display. Used sparingly for emphasis rather than hierarchy.

components.name: Hard Shadow Block
components.role: Editorial feature card with retro offset

components.name: Status Badge
components.role: Inline status indicator in product tables

components.name: Document Card
components.role: Content tile in galleries and resource grids

do: Use Calibre-R (or Manrope 800 substitute) at 52-72px with -0.035em to -0.045em tracking for all display headlines.
Anchor the primary CTA on a solid #000000 fill with white Inter 600 text, 8px radius, and a 1.5px inset #212121 shadow.
Open the page with a full-bleed #fff6ec hero band when the goal is brand introduction or top-of-funnel conversion.
Show product through browser-chrome mockups that overlap section boundaries, anchored by the soft two-layer rgba(0,0,0,0.06) shadow stack.
Reserve #ee5a29 for single-word emphasis, eyebrows, or small icon accents - never fills or large surfaces.
Use 8px radius as the universal default for cards, buttons, and images; reach for 12px only on large CTAs.
Let Inter at 400/600 carry every functional label; never let body weight climb above 700.
doNot: Don't introduce a second chromatic accent - the system is monochrome plus a single ember orange.
Don't use soft blurred drop-shadows on content cards; elevation is either the hard 8px/8px black offset or the two-layer rgba stack, nothing in between.
Don't set body or subheading text in Calibre-R - it belongs only at 38px and above, 700 weight only.
Don't apply rounded pill (9999px) radii to primary buttons; 8px is the system default.
Don't place white cards directly on the cream band without a visible border or shadow - the value difference is too subtle.
Don't use light grays (#8e8e8, #aeaeae) for primary text; reserve them for placeholder and disabled states only.
Don't break the 4px spacing grid - all padding, gaps, and margins should snap to 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32.
